How to do itPreacher Curl

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Middle of palm

Wrong: Wrist bent back

Right: Middle of palm

Wrong: Wrist curled

Arms on pad

Right
ARMS ON PAD
Wrong
ARMS OFF PAD

Right: Pad under the armpits, upper arms flat on the pad.

Wrong: Upper arms lifted off the pad, torso heaving back.

Sit with the pad top under your armpits and your chest on it.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Arms off padYour upper arms lift off the pad as you heave the bar.
  2. Torso heaves backYour torso rocks back off the pad to swing the bar up.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Underhand grip on the curl bar.

Keep the hands in line with the forearms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Upper arms leaving the pad

    Fix: Go lighter. Keep the arms on the pad, body still.

  • Seat too high or low

    Fix: Reset it so the pad top sits under your armpits.

  • Dropping fast into the bottom

    Fix: Lower slowly, past 90 degrees. Go lighter if you can't control it.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour seat height is off, or your arms leave the pad.

    FixReset the seat. Go lighter.

  • FixTurn back a little earlier. Lower slowly.

  • Usually meansYour wrists are bent up or down under load.

    FixStop and don't train through the pain. Keep the wrist straight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so your chest and upper arms touch the pad.

  2. 2

    Pad top under your armpits, arms straight. Not so high you hunch.

  3. 3

    Feet flat on the floor. Upper body active, not hanging.

  4. 4

    Take the bar with an underhand grip.

  5. 5

    Pick a weight you can lower under control.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heaving a heavy bar off the pad can put the front shoulder at risk.
  • A wrong seat height can shift stress onto the shoulder.
  • Across many activities, most biceps tendon tears happened palm-up, elbow nearly straight.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

Elbow pain

Severe pain and hard to move, heard a snap, changed shape, tingling, or numbness? Get it checked today.

No better after a few weeks? See a doctor.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

Grip

Underhand grip, palms up, hands about shoulder-width.

Keep the hand in line with the forearm.

Common handling mistakes

  • Arms straight at the bottom

    Fix: Limit the range. Keep the arm slightly bent between reps.

  • Upper arms travelling back

    Fix: Keep the upper arms still by your sides.

  • Swinging the body

    Fix: Use less weight and lift with control.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

  • Usually meansYour wrists are bent up or down under load.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the pulley to the lowest position and attach a bar.

  2. 2

    Take an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width.

  3. 3

    Step back from the stack. Stand upright, feet about hip-width.

  4. 4

    Pick a weight you can curl without swinging.

  5. 5

    Lift and lower under control, arms slightly bent at the bottom.

Risks and when to stop

  • Bent wrists under load can cause wrist discomfort.

How to do itBayesian Cable Curl

Upper arm

Right
UPPER ARM STILL
Wrong
UPPER ARM SWINGS

Right: Upper arm still and close, behind the torso. Lower slowly.

Wrong: Upper arm swinging forward as the handle rises.

Cable distance

Right
LIGHT TENSION
Wrong
ARM FAR BACK

Right: A step from the cable, light tension, modest stretch.

Wrong: Standing far away with the arm pulled far behind.

Start with the working arm drawn back behind your torso, cable taut.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Upper arm swingsYour upper arm swings forward so the shoulder helps lift the handle.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arm.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansSome tension here can come with the arm held back.

    FixStand closer if it is more than a stretch.

  • Usually meansHolding the arm back may stress the shoulder.

    FixStand closer to the cable, or choose another curl.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the cable to its lowest height with a single handle.

  2. 2

    Handle in your working hand, back to the machine.

  3. 3

    Step forward to light tension, arm behind you, torso leaning slightly forward.

  4. 4

    Stand closer if your shoulder feels restricted.

  5. 5

    Brace the trunk, no tilting. Free hand on your hip.

Risks and when to stop

  • Holding the arm behind the body can cause shoulder discomfort for some people.

Right

Wrong

Common handling mistakes

  • Elbow wedged into the knee

    Fix: Press the triceps into your inner thigh instead.

  • Curling up to the shoulder

    Fix: Stop when the upper arm starts to leave vertical.

  • Letting the weight drop

    Fix: Lower slowly. Resist the weight.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arm and your forearm.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe elbow is wedged into the knee.

    FixMove the upper arm onto the inner thigh.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Pick a dumbbell several pounds lighter than for your usual curls.

  2. 2

    Sit on the bench edge, knees wide.

  3. 3

    Hinge forward with a neutral spine.

  4. 4

    Rest the back of your upper arm on your inner thigh.

  5. 5

    Feet pressed down. Free hand on your other knee or the bench.

    How to do itDumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension

    Upper arm position

    Right
    ARMS VERTICAL
    Wrong
    ARMS DROPPED BACK

    Right: Upper arms vertical, dumbbell clear of the head at 90°.

    Wrong: Upper arms dropped back.

    Keep the upper arms vertical and still. Only the elbows bend.

    Saved offline
    Tells
    1. Back archesYour lower back arches as you press the dumbbell up.
    Press1 s
    Hold1 s
    Lower2 s
    Look closer

    Grip

    One dumbbell, both hands wrapped round the handle. Palms up, dumbbell hanging vertically.

    Keep your wrists still throughout.

    Common handling mistakes

    • Arching the back

      Fix: Brace. If the back still arches, use a lighter dumbbell.

    • Elbows flare, upper arms move

      Fix: Keep upper arms vertical, elbows shoulder-width. Stop lowering if they move.

    • Swinging the weight with momentum

      Fix: Slow down, no momentum. Keep head, torso, wrists and feet still.

    Where you should feel it

    You should feel this in the back of your upper arms.

    MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
    If you feel it in…

    • Usually meansYou are arching your back.

      FixBrace and use a lighter dumbbell.

    • Usually meansYou arch your back under a heavy weight.

      FixUse a lighter dumbbell.

    • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

    Set it up

    1. 1

      Pick a dumbbell you can get overhead safely.

    2. 2

      Stand in a split stance, or sit on a back-supported bench.

    3. 3

      Wrap both hands round the handle, dumbbell hanging vertically.

    4. 4

      Brace. Arms vertical, dumbbell over your head, elbows forward, not locked.

    5. 5

      For heavy sets, a spotter can help by supporting your elbows.

    Risks and when to stop

    • Across weight training, dropped weights are the most common way people get badly hurt.
    • Triceps tendon rupture (rare), often from forceful lowering or lifting against resistance.
    • Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

    Grip

    Closed neutral grip, palms facing your body, thumbs round the handles.

    Keep the wrist straight, with no bend or twist.

    Common handling mistakes

    • Arm fully straight at bottom

      Fix: Limit the range. Keep the arm slightly bent between reps.

    • Swinging the dumbbells with momentum

      Fix: Go lighter and control the weight. A seated version helps stop swinging.

    • Shrugging the shoulder

      Fix: Keep the shoulders down and back.

    1. 1

      Pick a weight you can lift without swinging.

    2. 2

      Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart.

    3. 3

      Hold the dumbbells in front of you, palms facing your body.

    4. 4

      Brace your trunk upright, shoulders down, lower back not arched.

    5. 5

      Curl toward the opposite shoulder. Lower the same path, then switch.

    Risks and when to stop

    • Swinging the dumbbells raises the risk of injury.
    • Across weight training, dropped weights are the most common way people get badly hurt.

    How to do itWrist Curl

    Forearm support

    Right
    FOREARM ON THIGH
    Wrong
    ARM STRAIGHTENS

    Right: Forearm flat on the thigh, only the hand moving.

    Wrong: Arms extending or body leaning forward to move the weight.

    Rest the forearm on your thigh. Only the hand moves.

    Saved offline
    Tells
    1. Body leans inYour body leans forward to help move the weight.
    2. Arm straightensYour arm straightens and the forearm lifts off the thigh.
    Curl2 s
    Lower2 s
    Look closer

    Grip

    Palm up, closed fist around the handle. Never let it roll to the fingertips.

    Common handling mistakes

    • Weight rolling to the fingertips

      Fix: Squeeze the weight hard both ways.

    • Leaning or straightening the arms

      Fix: Keep the forearm down.

    • Going heavy over the edge

      Fix: Stay light. Add reps before weight.

    Where you should feel it

    You should feel this along the palm-up side of your forearms.

    MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
    If you feel it in…

    • Usually meansThe weight is too heavy, or your grip is opening.

      FixGo lighter and keep the fist closed.

    Set it up

    1. 1

      Pick a light weight you can move for 15-20 reps.

    2. 2

      Sit, forearm on your thigh or a bench, hand past the edge.

    3. 3

      Hold the dumbbell palm up in a closed grip.

    4. 4

      Lower slowly and hold briefly. Curl the wrist back up slowly.

    Risks and when to stop

    • Loosening the grip raises the risk of wrist injury and a dropped weight.
    • Hands over an edge leave the wrists vulnerable to heavy weight.

    Common handling mistakes

    • Elbows moving forward or back

      Fix: Keep the elbows at your sides.

    • Wrists twisting out of neutral

      Fix: Keep the palms facing your body the whole way.

    • Swinging the body

      Fix: Take weight off and lift with control.

    Where you should feel it

    You should feel this in the front of your upper arm and your forearm.

    MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
    If you feel it in…

    2. 2

      Take a split stance, brace, shoulders down and back.

    3. 3

      Hold the dumbbells with a closed neutral grip beside your thighs.

    4. 4

      Curl to the front of the shoulders, lower to straight arms.

    5. 5

      Torso upright, no arching the lower back, no shrugging.

    Risks and when to stop

    • Too heavy a weight can make you swing and cut reps short.

    How to do itSingle-Arm Triceps Pushdown

    Elbow position

    Right
    ELBOW AT SIDE
    Wrong
    DRIFTED FORWARD

    Right: Working elbow against the side at the top.

    Wrong: Elbow drifted forward, upper arm swung up.

    Keep the working upper arm at your side so only the forearm moves.

    Saved offline
    Tells
    1. Leaning overYou lean over the handle or arch your back to push it down.
    Press1 s
    Hold1 s
    Return2 s
    Look closer

    Grip

    Single handle, firm full grip, thumb wrapped.

    Keep the wrist in line with the forearm.

    Common handling mistakes

    • Leaning over or arching back

      Fix: Tilt from your hips. Don't arch your back.

    • Elbow drifting forward

      Fix: Keep the elbow at your side. Stop the return at upper-chest level.

    • Turning the torso

      Fix: Keep shoulders and hips square.

    Where you should feel it

    You should feel this in the back of your upper arm.

    MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
    If you feel it in…

    • Usually meansYour elbow drifts forward, which brings in the lats.

      FixPin the elbow to your side.

    • FixStop and don't train through the pain. Use lighter weights for more reps.

    • FixStop and don't train through the pain. Stand taller, tilt only from the hips.

    Set it up

    1. 1

      Set the pulley above head height and attach a single handle.

    2. 2

      Grip the handle firmly, thumb wrapped.

    3. 3

      Stand facing the machine with your shoulders and hips square.

    4. 4

      Brace, torso upright. Working elbow at your side, hand at upper chest.

    5. 5

      Straighten the arm fully without locking the elbow.

    Risks and when to stop

    • Heavy loads feel uncomfortable in the elbows for many people.
    • Too much weight moved with momentum can lead to injury.
    • Leaning or arching can strain the lower back.

      Lower the bar slowly, keeping tension at the bottom. No half reps.

    Common handling mistakes

    • Swinging to move the bar

      Fix: Go lighter and control both the lift and the lowering.

    • Wrists bending under the bar

      Fix: Keep the wrists neutral.

      Fix: Reduce the weight. Keep the elbows close to your ribs.

    1. 1

      Start light. Add weight as you get stronger.

    2. 2

      Stand with feet hip- to shoulder-width, knees soft.

    4. 4

      Stand tall, no arching. Shoulders back and down, chin slightly tucked.

    5. 5

      Lower the bar slowly, keeping tension at the bottom.
